mechanism_narrative: A consistently high federal funds rate (above 4.5%) is associated with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days, and this relationship holds without requiring a threshold crossing condition to activate the signal.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of the periods when FEDFUNDS is above 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A CPIAUCSL index reading above 200 indicates persistent high inflation, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL > 200 does not lead to negative returns in more than 50% of the cases over a 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates a weakening demand cycle, which predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: The joint decline in HOUST and RSAFS does not lead to negative returns in more than 50% of the cases over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a labor market with low unemployment (UNRATE < 4.0%) and strong job growth (PAYEMS > 100k), the S&P 500 tends to produce positive returns over the next 60 days as the economy approaches a peak.
failure_condition: The condition UNRATE < 4.0% and PAYEMS > 100k does not lead to positive returns in more than 50% of the cases over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO < 110.0) signals a weakening supply chain, which predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: INDPRO < 110.0 does not lead to negative returns in more than 50% of the cases over a 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained high level of the CPI index (CPIAUCSL > 200) is associated with negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days, and this relationship is always active.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL > 200 does not lead to negative returns in more than 50% of the cases over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate (UNRATE > 4.5% and increasing by more than 0.2pp in a month) signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: The condition UNRATE > 4.5% and UNRATE increase > 0.2pp does not lead to negative returns in more than 50% of the cases over a 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts (HOUST) and quarterly GDP growth (GDPC1) indicates a strong economic expansion, which predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: The joint increase in HOUST and GDPC1 does not lead to positive returns in more than 50% of the cases over a 3-year rolling window.
